Sarvam Kaze glasses · audio prototype v0.14 (org edition)

Kaze Sound Kit

The proposed 15 sounds for Kaze, each with several options to choose from, and the key interaction flows that use them. Pick an option on any sound and the flows use it straight away. The Indic options model santoor, sitar, tanpura, veena, tabla, bansuri, ghatam and jal tarang in code, using the notes of Raag Bhupali. Every sound on this page is generated by code in the browser, with no third party recordings, and every option can be downloaded as a WAV file.

    Appendix

    Assumptions in this prototype

    Open decisions, set to a default here

    • No wake word. Kaze starts from a touch on the frame. Tap to talk and press and hold to talk are both modelled; switch above.
    • "Searching" filler is off by default. Toggle above to compare.
    • A tap while Kaze is thinking or speaking cancels. A tap during a call alert answers it.
    • After a call, the interrupted answer resumes.

    Indic option guardrails

    • No shankh, temple bells, aarti or Om. Kaze is an everyday product for users of every faith.
    • Instruments drawn from both traditions: santoor, tabla and bansuri (Hindustani), veena and ghatam (Carnatic), plus tanpura and jal tarang.
    • Short and restrained. The instrument gives the colour; timing rules are the same for every option.
    • Avoid the film score "exotic India" sitar cliché. Sitar is used only for tiny glides.

    What a good thinking sound needs

    • Says "working, not stuck": it keeps changing over time instead of sitting still.
    • Has no steady beat. A countable rhythm makes a wait feel longer.
    • Stays in the background: quiet, soft edges, below speech, never mistaken for an alert or a notification.
    • Sounds like a capable, modern assistant at work: precise, warm and purposeful. Not meditative, organic or bodily, and not a machine ticking.
    • Feels connected to the listening chime, so listening, thinking and answering read as one flow. Indian instruments are an accent, not the whole identity.
    • Tolerable many times a day, for 2 to 15 s at a time.
    • Starts quickly, fades out cleanly before the answer, and is audible outdoors on small speakers.

    Timing rules used

    • Listening chime within 100 ms of the touch.
    • Tap to talk: 0.7 s of silence ends the question. No speech for 5 s closes the session with the cancel sound. Press and hold: letting go ends the question.
    • The thinking sound starts only if the answer takes longer than the silence set at the top (1.5 s by default, adjustable from 0 to 3 s). Short answers stay silent. Adjust its pace with the loop cycle slider; changes apply from the next cycle.
    • "Still working on it" at 8 s. Error and timeout at 15 s.
    • Loop fades out over 150 ms before the answer. No "answer starting" sound.

    Kaze Sound Kit, org edition, 17 Sep 2026. Opens in any modern browser; sounds are generated live, voices are Sarvam Bulbul recordings built into the file, and fonts need an internet connection.
